messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: High error rate on serving-runtime (model-serving-prod) — spike in CUDA Illegal Memory Access errors and container OOMs. Metrics: 5xx rate 18% -> 45% over last 3m. Linked: http://observability/alerts/1769004321 :rotating_light:

alice (oncall): hitting this now, seeing a cluster of node flaps and container restarts. low-traffic but multiple customers affected. triage status?

alice (oncall): I see repeated `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` in logs and some containers OOMing immediately after.

ops-bot: auto-run: collected diagnostics bundle -> /artifacts/1769004321/diag.tar.gz. Running `kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=model-serving -o wide` snapshot attached.

alice (oncall): @dmitri can you take lead on node-level triage? i'll coordinate with runtime eng for mitigations.

dmitri (sre): on it. initial look: two nodes in pool-gpu-1 rebooted (killed by kubelet -> node transient NotReady) around same time window. Node events show container OOMKill then kernel messages about invalid device address.

ben (runtime): joining. we saw a recent rollout of the optimized attention kernel last night (canary -> main). rolling restart started ~02:10 UTC. timeline match?

carla (platform): yes, that rollout touched runtime image tag rtf-optim-2026-03-14-7. we pinned it but auto-batch jobs might still hit new kernels.

mika (cs): CS update: two mid-market customers reported degraded responses (timeouts / 5xx) starting ~02:12 UTC. need a short customer-facing note if we expect >30m.

alice (oncall): quick snapshot of logs (cropped):
```
[model-serving] ERROR: generation failed: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
E 1769004323.112 kernel: NVRM: GPU 0: Xid (PCIe) 31: PID 24523: Illegal address
container runtime: oom-kill event: process 24523 (server) killed by SIGKILL
stacktrace:
  at aten::cuda::native_kernel_fun
  at lll_attention_kernel::run
```

ben (runtime): that `Xid 31` line is consistent with misaligned device address on our driver/kernel combo. Could be a race in KV cache eviction + attention kernel.

dmitri (sre): reproducer attempts on a repro node show the same backtrace when running concurrent long-context requests + forced eviction. I can repro ~30% of runs.

alice (oncall): customer impact: 2 customers throttled, a handful of anonymous requests errored. SLA pager not triggered yet but keep me posted.

carla (platform): immediate mitigation options: 1) cordon affected nodes and drain (evac) 2) roll back runtime image to previous stable tag rtf-optim-2026-03-13-2 3) apply a hot runtime config to reduce concurrent KV evictions (`KV_CACHE_MAX_EVICT=1`) 4) fallback routing to cpu-backed replicas for affected routes.

ben (runtime): preference is 3 + 4 immediately. rollback (2) is heavier — may cause extra restarts and transient errors. 3 reduces concurrency surface and is reversible. we can also disable the new fused attention path via ENV `FORCE_LEGACY_ATTENTION=1` for a narrower mitigation.

dmitri (sre): starting cordon of the two noisy nodes to stop new pods landing. will drain if safe. cordon done.

alice (oncall): @ben please push config change to runtime via our config manager (prod/runtime/overrides) with TTL 30m. I'll coordinate drain windows.

ben (runtime): pushed `FORCE_LEGACY_ATTENTION=1` and `KV_CACHE_MAX_EVICT=1` to prod runtime override. rollout to pods in progress.

ops-bot: config apply: prod/runtime/overrides updated by ben at 1769004380. Noted.

alice (oncall): observing metrics... 5xx down from 45% -> 12% over 6m. pods restart rate reduced.

mika (cs): thanks. I'll message affected customers with an initial note: brief incident, we have mitigation in place, investigating root cause. Suggest follow-up once stabilised.

carla (platform): we should still avoid full rollback unless errors spike back. also preparing routing rule to move 10% of traffic to cpu-fallback pool for the most sensitive customers.

dmitri (sre): draining one node now to repro with an isolated workload; collecting `dmesg` and nvidia bug reports for eng. dmesg excerpt: 
```
[ 1023.451234] NVRM: Xid (PCIe) 31 detected on GPU 0000:3b:00.0
[ 1023.451237] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1023.451240] kernel: NVRM: GPU 0: failed pagewalk: misaligned device address
```

ben (runtime): can you dump the exact kernel module versions and cu driver? I want to check known Xid 31 signatures. Also capture `nv bug-report` outputs.

dmitri (sre): nv driver: 525.85.12, kernel: 5.15.0-rt, runtime image: rtf-optim-2026-03-14-7. Files uploaded to /artifacts/1769004321/bugs/

alice (oncall): short plan: 1) keep overrides active for 60m 2) cordon noisy nodes until we have a driver/kernel mitigation or rollback decision 3) eng to investigate kernel/race; if rollback needed we'll schedule controlled rollback 4) CS to notify customers with ETA 120m

ben (runtime): action: i'll reproduce with sanitizers on a repro node (disable pooling too) and add additional checks to kv eviction. If we can't root-cause quickly propose staged rollback to previous runtime by rolling one pool at a time.

mika (cs): customer note drafted: "We're aware of increased errors affecting text-generation for some customers. We've applied temporary mitigations and are continuing our investigation. We will follow up in 2 hours with more details." approve?

alice (oncall): approve. send now.

mika (cs): sent to affected contacts at 1769004472.

ops-bot: gauge: incident_severity -> P2 (set by alice).

carla (platform): routing rule in place to shift 10% traffic to cpu-fallback for routes: /v1/generate and /v1/chat/completions (applied at 1769004499).

alice (oncall): monitoring: token latency stable, error rate trending down. No new node reboots in last 8m. Keeping cordon.

dmitri (sre): collected nv bug reports + core dumps. attaching to issue #INC-1769004321 in tracker.

ben (runtime): quick find: the fused attention path allocates a temporary GPU buffer and sometimes races with KV cache reclaim under heavy concurrency — frees memory while kernel still touched it. adding a memory fence and delaying free seems to stop the repro locally. i'll open a PR for a conservative fix and a test harness for long-context concurrent workloads.

alice (oncall): good. next steps to close incident: 1) keep mitigations 60m 2) validate no regressions 3) plan either staged rollback or merge + deploy conservative fix 4) post-incident RCA within 48h with timeline and customer impact.

mika (cs): will follow up with customers after RCA.

carla (platform): I'll prepare a controlled rollback playbook if we choose that route.

ben (runtime): PR created: rtf/patches#987 - includes memory fence + extra test. tagging @carla for canary rollout plan.

alice (oncall): lowered alert threshold to warn. leaving thread open for updates. great coordination. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigations applied, error rate decreasing, P2. Next automated update in 30m unless manually changed.

alice (oncall): closing operational loop for now. will re-open if we see re-occurence. drafting handoff note for next oncall: summary + where artifacts are.

alice (oncall): handoff snippet for next shift: "Applied FORCE_LEGACY_ATTENTION and KV_CACHE_MAX_EVICT, cordoned 2 nodes (IDs: gpu-12, gpu-17). Repro confirmed locally; eng has a PR with conservative fix. Artifacts: /artifacts/1769004321. Customer notifications sent. Monitor metrics and keep cordon until root cause patch or rollback scheduled."

dmitri (sre): ack. I'll keep the cordon until eng verifies the patch in canary and we validate stability.

mika (cs): ack. will wait for RCA before final customer follow-up.

ben (runtime): rolling canary with the patch queued for 1769005000 window.

alice (oncall): last note: if errors spike again, escalate to P1 and we'll initiate rollback.
